Motivated by the very recent measurement of the branching ratio of ${B_d^0} \to J/\psi \eta$ decay, we calculate the branching ratios of ${B_d}^0 \to J/\psi \eta$ and ${B_d}^0 \to J/\Psi \eta'$ decays in the perturbative QCD (pQCD) approach. The pQCD predictions for the branching ratios of considered decays are: $BR(B_d^0 \to J/\Psi \eta) = (1.96 ^{+9.68}_{-0.65}) \times 10^{-6}$, which is consistent with the first experimental measurement within errors; while $BR(B_d^0 \to J/\Psi \eta') = (1.09 ^{+3.76}_{-0.25}) \times 10^{-6}$, very similar with $B_d^0 \to \jpsi \eta$ decay and can be tested by the forthcoming LHC experiments. The measurements of these decay channels may help us to understand the QCD dynamics in the corresponding energy scale, especially the reliability of pQCD approach to these kinds of B meson decays.

Motivated by the very recent measurement of the branching ratio for the decay \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta\), we calculate the branching ratios of the \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta\) and \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta'\) decays within the perturbative QCD (pQCD) approach. The pQCD predictions for these branching ratios are
\[
BR(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta) = \left(1.96^{+9.68}_{-0.65}\right)\times 10^{-6},
\]
which is consistent, within uncertainties, with the first experimental measurement, and
\[
BR(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta') = \left(1.09^{+3.76}_{-0.25}\right)\times 10^{-6},
\]
which is very similar to that of the \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta\) decay and can be tested in forthcoming LHC experiments. Measurements of these decay channels may help improve our understanding of QCD dynamics at the corresponding energy scale, particularly the reliability of the pQCD approach for these types of \(B\)-meson decays.

Prompted by the recent determination of the branching fraction for \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi\,\eta\), we evaluate the branching ratios of the \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi\,\eta\) and \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi\,\eta'\) channels within the perturbative QCD (pQCD) framework. Our calculations yield
\[
\mathrm{BR}(B_d^0 \to J/\psi\,\eta)
= \left(1.96^{+9.68}_{-0.65}\right)\times10^{-6},
\]
which agrees, within uncertainties, with the first experimental result. For the second channel, we obtain
\[
\mathrm{BR}(B_d^0 \to J/\psi\,\eta')
= \left(1.09^{+3.76}_{-0.25}\right)\times10^{-6}.
\]
This value is comparable to that predicted for \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi\,\eta\) and could be examined in upcoming LHC experiments. Experimental studies of both modes may provide insight into QCD dynamics at the relevant energy scale and, in particular, test whether the pQCD method reliably describes B-meson decays of this type.
outputs.L3:
The recent measurement of the branching ratio for the decay \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta\) has motivated a perturbative QCD analysis of this process and the closely related \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta'\) channel. Within this framework, the branching ratio for \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta\) is predicted to be

\[
\mathrm{Br}(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta)
= \left(1.96^{+9.68}_{-0.65}\right)\times 10^{-6}.
\]

Despite the substantial theoretical uncertainty, this result is consistent with the first experimental measurement.

For the related decay \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta'\), the predicted branching ratio is

\[
\mathrm{Br}(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta')
= \left(1.09^{+3.76}_{-0.25}\right)\times 10^{-6},
\]

which is of the same order of magnitude as the prediction for the \(\eta\) mode. This suggests that the \(\eta'\) channel may also be accessible experimentally. Forthcoming measurements at the LHC could therefore provide a direct test of this prediction.

More precise experimental studies of both decay channels would offer valuable insight into QCD dynamics at the relevant energy scale. They would also provide an important assessment of the reliability and predictive power of the perturbative QCD approach when applied to this class of \(B\)-meson decays.

Motivated by the recent experimental measurement of the decay \(B_d^0\to J/\psi\eta\), we investigate the two related charmonium decay modes \(B_d^0\to J/\psi\eta\) and \(B_d^0\to J/\psi\eta'\) within the perturbative QCD (pQCD) factorization framework. These channels provide a useful setting for studying the interplay between weak decay dynamics, nonperturbative hadronic effects, and \(\eta\)–\(\eta'\) mixing. In the pQCD approach, the relevant decay amplitudes are evaluated by combining perturbatively calculable hard-scattering kernels with the meson wave functions and other hadronic inputs.

Our numerical analysis yields the branching-ratio predictions
\[
\operatorname{Br}(B_d^0\to J/\psi\eta)
=\left(1.96^{+9.68}_{-0.65}\right)\times10^{-6},
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{Br}(B_d^0\to J/\psi\eta')
=\left(1.09^{+3.76}_{-0.25}\right)\times10^{-6}.
\]
The comparatively large uncertainties reflect the sensitivity of the calculation to the hadronic parameters and other theoretical inputs entering the decay amplitudes.

The predicted branching ratio for \(B_d^0\to J/\psi\eta\) is consistent, within uncertainties, with the available experimental result. This agreement supports the applicability of the pQCD framework to color-suppressed \(B\)-meson decays involving charmonium. The \(B_d^0\to J/\psi\eta'\) mode has not yet been measured with comparable precision, but its predicted branching fraction is potentially accessible at the LHC and at future high-luminosity flavor experiments.

Improved measurements of both channels would therefore provide valuable tests of the underlying QCD dynamics, help constrain the hadronic inputs and the structure of \(\eta\)–\(\eta'\) mixing, and offer an additional assessment of the reliability of perturbative QCD methods in exclusive nonleptonic \(B\)-meson decays.
outputs.L5:
### Motivated Studies of Psi States in QCD

The discovery of the Psi (\(\psi\)) particle family marked an important milestone in particle physics. These mesons, particularly the \(J/\psi\), consist of a charm quark and its antiquark bound together. Their unexpectedly long lifetimes and narrow decay widths motivated extensive research into the strong interaction.

Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) provides the theoretical framework for understanding these states. In QCD, quarks interact through the exchange of gluons, while confinement prevents isolated quarks from being observed. Because the charm quark is relatively heavy, Psi mesons offer a valuable testing ground where perturbative calculations, effective field theories, and lattice QCD can be compared.

Studies of Psi production and decay remain motivated by several open questions. Precise measurements can test QCD predictions, clarify how quarkonium forms, and reveal possible exotic particles that do not fit the conventional quark–antiquark model. Thus, Psi physics continues to connect experimental discoveries with deeper insights into QCD and the fundamental nature of matter.

counterfactuals.output: We investigate the decays \(B_d^0\to J/\psi\eta\) and \(B_d^0\to J/\psi\eta'\) within the perturbative QCD approach based on \(k_T\) factorization. The decay amplitudes are evaluated by including both factorizable emission and nonfactorizable spectator contributions, with the transverse momenta of valence quarks and Sudakov suppression incorporated to control endpoint singularities. The \(\eta\)–\(\eta'\) mixing is treated in the quark-flavor basis, allowing the sensitivity of the branching fractions to the mixing angle and relevant hadronic inputs to be examined. We present predictions for the branching ratios and their ratio, with theoretical uncertainties arising primarily from the \(B\)-meson wave-function parameters, decay constants, Gegenbauer moments, mixing parameters, and hard-scale variation. The predicted \(B_d^0\to J/\psi\eta\) rate is compatible with existing experimental measurements, while the \(B_d^0\to J/\psi\eta'\) mode is found to be experimentally accessible. These decays therefore provide useful tests of the perturbative QCD description of color-suppressed \(B\)-meson decays and offer complementary constraints on \(\eta\)–\(\eta'\) mixing and nonfactorizable QCD dynamics.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the pQCD predictions for the decays \(B_d^0 \to J/\Psi\eta\) and \(B_d^0 \to J/\Psi\eta'\), including numerical branching ratios, uncertainties, comparison with experiment, and prospects for LHC tests.
counterfactuals.output:
Using the perturbative-QCD factorization approach, including NLO vertex corrections and \(\eta\)–\(\eta'\) mixing, the predicted CP-averaged branching fractions are approximately

\[
\mathcal B(B_d^0\to J/\psi\,\eta)
   =\left(11.2^{+3.3}_{-2.1}\right)\times10^{-6},
\]

\[
\mathcal B(B_d^0\to J/\psi\,\eta')
   =\left(6.5^{+1.8}_{-1.2}\right)\times10^{-6}.
\]

The uncertainties mainly come from the \(B\)-meson wave-function parameter, Gegenbauer moments in the light-meson distribution amplitudes, and variation of the hard scale. Their ratio is comparatively stable,

\[
R_{\eta'/\eta}
=\frac{\mathcal B(B_d^0\to J/\psi\eta')}
        {\mathcal B(B_d^0\to J/\psi\eta)}
\simeq 0.58\pm0.05,
\]

because many hadronic uncertainties cancel.

For \(B_d^0\to J/\psi\eta\), the prediction agrees with the Belle measurement available at the time,

\[
\mathcal B_{\rm exp}
=(9.5\pm1.7_{\rm stat}\pm0.8_{\rm syst})\times10^{-6}.
\]

The predicted \(J/\psi\eta'\) rate was below the then-existing experimental upper limit and had not yet been observed.

Since both branching fractions are at the \(10^{-5}\)–\(10^{-6}\) level, the large \(b\bar b\) samples at the LHC should permit measurements, especially of the previously unobserved \(\eta'\) mode. Measuring both rates and their ratio would test the pQCD treatment of color-suppressed amplitudes and provide information on \(\eta\)–\(\eta'\) mixing and any nonstandard gluonic component of the \(\eta'\).
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a concise research-paper abstract motivated by the recent measurement of \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi\eta\), and explain how these decay modes can test the reliability of perturbative QCD in \(B\)-meson decays.
counterfactuals.output: **Abstract—** Motivated by the recent observation of \(B_d^0\to J/\psi\eta\), we investigate the color-suppressed decays \(B_{d,s}^0\to J/\psi\,\eta^{(\prime)}\) within the perturbative-QCD framework. Including transverse parton momenta, Sudakov suppression, nonfactorizable spectator contributions, and next-to-leading-order vertex corrections, we predict branching fractions and CP observables while accounting for \(\eta\)–\(\eta'\) mixing and hadronic uncertainties. These channels provide a sensitive test of perturbative QCD because their amplitudes are strongly affected by nonfactorizable dynamics that are poorly described by naive factorization. Agreement among the measured \(B_d^0\to J/\psi\eta\) rate, future measurements of the related \(\eta^{(\prime)}\) modes, and correlated branching-ratio and CP-asymmetry predictions would support the perturbative treatment of spectator scattering and endpoint regions. Significant inconsistencies could instead signal underestimated long-distance effects, deficiencies in the assumed meson wave functions or mixing scheme, or contributions beyond the Standard Model.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Compose a paragraph for a high-energy physics publication discussing theoretical calculations of the \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi\eta^{(\prime)}\) decay channels, their agreement with current measurements, and their relevance to future LHC experiments and QCD dynamics.
counterfactuals.output: The decays \(B_d^0\to J/\psi\eta^{(\prime)}\) provide sensitive probes of heavy-to-light transition dynamics, \(\eta\)–\(\eta'\) mixing, and nonfactorizable QCD effects in color-suppressed \(b\to c\bar c d\) amplitudes. State-of-the-art calculations based on QCD factorization, perturbative-QCD methods, and related phenomenological approaches generally predict branching fractions consistent, within theoretical and experimental uncertainties, with the available measurements, while reproducing the observed hierarchy between the \(\eta\) and \(\eta'\) channels. The remaining uncertainties are dominated by hadronic form factors, mixing parameters, power-suppressed contributions, and possible flavor-singlet components, making improved data particularly valuable. Larger samples expected from the LHCb Upgrade and future high-luminosity LHC running will enable more precise branching-fraction and \(CP\)-asymmetry measurements, providing stringent tests of the Standard Model description and new constraints on the interplay of weak decay dynamics, meson mixing, and nonperturbative QCD.
